headline: Onboard subject to conditions: identification, operating evidence and screening are all complete, and the liens and litigation that looked adverse resolve on reading — what remains is the adverse media source, the ownership certification and a standing certificate.

body.text: This file is in better shape than its headline counts suggested. Reading the actual filings in Adverse information turned eight of the ten liens and all ten litigations into other companies' business: closed state tax liens, a foreclosure naming fifteen defendants, a run of Georgia cases sharing one party. What is genuinely outstanding is three things of three different kinds. One is a finding nobody has read — the high risk adverse media source, and it is now the only uncharacterised item in the file. One is a document only the customer can supply: the beneficial-ownership certification, since nothing publishes owners. One is a certificate the state of formation will not publish and the customer must obtain. The two open UCC filings are worth a question to the secured parties rather than a condition, since neither states a sum and one names an unrelated co-debtor.

followUps.text: Pull the adverse media source and read it, since it is now the only finding on the file carrying a score without an article behind it.
Collect a signed beneficial-ownership certification naming every natural person owning 25 percent or more, then screen each against watchlists and PEP lists as the matched officer already was.
Request a Certificate of Good Standing for the state of formation from the customer, which is the only evidence of standing available because the state publishes none.
Ask the two secured parties on the open UCC filings what they secure and for how much, and confirm the Virginia filing is not a debtor-name collision given the secured party's line of work.

Ask the customer why the submitted individual is not named on the company's own website when the state filings list them as an officer — a question about the application rather than about the business.

Assemble the case file in stage order — identification, the ownership certification, the standing and operating evidence, then the screening and adverse dispositions with the lien and litigation readings attached — and date-stamp each item for the next periodic review.
Set the monitoring terms before the account funds: refresh liens, litigation and adverse media on a fixed cycle, and treat a change in registration status or a new officer as a trigger for re-review.
